{{Short description|Mathematical analysis of game mechanics}}
'''Theorycraft''' (or '''theorycrafting''') is the mathematical analysis of [[game mechanics]] (usually in [[video games]]) to discover optimal [[Strategy|strategies]] and [[Tactic (method)|tactics]]. Theorycraft involves analyzing [[statistics]], hidden [[System|systems]] or underlying game [[Source code|code]] in order to glean information that is not apparent during normal [[gameplay]].<ref name="Nardi2010">{{cite book|author=Bonnie Nardi|title=My Life as a Night Elf Priest: An Anthropological Account of World of Warcraft|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8Ac9pUyROE8C&pg=PA137|date=2 June 2010|publisher=University of Michigan Press|isbn=978-0-472-02671-5|pages=137–142}}</ref>  Theorycraft is similar to analyses performed in sports or other games such as baseball's [[sabermetrics]]. The term has been said to come from [[StarCraft]] players as a [[portmanteau]] of "[[game theory]]" and "StarCraft".<ref name="wowwiki">{{cite web |url=http://www.wowwiki.com/Theorycraft |title=Theorycraft |access-date=13 March 2016 |quote=The term originated in the StarCraft community as composite colloquialism between the name StarCraft and Game Theory.}}</ref>

Theorycraft is prominent in [[competitive gaming]] (such as [[multiplayer video game|multiplayer games]], [[speedrunning]] and [[racing]] events), where players attempt to gain competitive advantage by analyzing game systems. As a result, theorycraft can lower barriers between players and [[Game design|game designers]]. Game designers must consider that players will have a comprehensive understanding of game systems and players can influence design by exploiting game systems and discovering dominant or unintended strategies.<ref name="game studies">{{cite journal |url=http://gamestudies.org/1102/articles/paul |title=Optimizing Play: How Theorycraft Changes Gameplay and Design |journal=Game Studies |date=May 2011 |volume=11 |issue=2 |access-date=13 March 2016 |quote=The growth in the role of theorycrafting offers room to analyze how games change over time and how players can influence a game's design by reshaping how they play.. |last1=Paul |first1=Christopher A. }}</ref>

Theorycrafting proven to be potent usually finds inclusion in [[Metagaming|the metagame]]. Theorycrafting knowledge is often communicated through [[Online community|online communities]].<ref name="wowwiki" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ask |first=Kristine |date=February 7, 2017 |title=The Value of Calculations: The Coproduction of Theorycraft and Player Practices |url=https://brage.bibsys.no/xmlui/bitstream/handle/11250/2458233/The%2Bvalue%2Bof%2Bcalculations%2Bpostprint.pdf?sequence=2 |journal=Bulletin of Science, Technology & Society |volume=36 |issue=3 |pages=190–200 |doi=10.1177/0270467617690058 |s2cid=151535702 |hdl-access=free |hdl=11250/2458233}}</ref>

The way players theorycraft varies from game to game but often games under the same [[Video game genre|genres]] will have similar theorycrafting methods. Communities develop standardized ways to communicate their findings, including use of specialized tools to measure and record game data; terminology; and simulations to represent certain data.

The term theorycraft can be used in a pejorative sense.<ref name="game studies"></ref> In this sense, "theorycraft" refers to naïve or impractical theorizing that would not succeed during actual gameplay.
